items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This update addresses 11 vulnerabilities, including 5 Critical, 5 High, and 1 Medium, which could lead to arbitrary code execution, privilege escalation, arbitrary file system writes, and security feature bypass. The most severe, CVE-2026-103849, is an unauthenticated template injection with a CVSS score of 10.0.

items.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine (BlockStrap)
items.summary: Dubbed 'BlockStrap' by Sansec, this maximum-severity vulnerability (CVSS 10.0) allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary PHP code on Magento and Adobe Commerce servers. It was part of the APSB26-153 October 2026 security update.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source (StyleSmuggler)
items.summary: This critical zero-day vulnerability, named 'StyleSmuggler,' allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution and has been actively exploited in the wild to install remote access trojans. Adobe released an emergency hotfix for this issue.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source
items.summary: This update resolves seven vulnerabilities, including a critical unauthenticated customer account takeover (CVE-2026-71362) that allows attackers to switch customer sessions and access private data. CVE-2026-71362 has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

items.title: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type (PolyShell)
items.summary: Dubbed 'PolyShell,' this unrestricted file upload flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to upload disguised image files containing PHP code, leading to arbitrary code execution. It was fixed in the August 2026 patch set and has been actively exploited in the wild, added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities.
